summary: Magdalena Mountains site in Socorro County; FFLA lists a crow's nest, now gone; no build or staffing history found; the area now hosts Langmuir Laboratory research.

facts.design: crow's nest type per FFLA; no design details found in the sources read
facts.status_note: FFLA lists the site as gone, with no date; no account of its removal found

evidence.supports: South Baldy site in Socorro County, crow's nest type, now gone
evidence.quote: South Baldy Socorro 33.99100 -107.18792 Crows Nest Gone

evidence.supports: South Baldy is the highest point of the Magdalena Mountains, 10,783 ft, and the tallest peak in Socorro County
evidence.quote: The highest point in the range is South Baldy, at 10,783 ft (3,287 m), which is also the tallest peak in Socorro County.

evidence.supports: most of the range is in the Magdalena Ranger District of the Cibola National Forest
evidence.quote: Most of the Magdalena Mountains are within the Magdalena Ranger District of the Cibola National Forest

evidence.supports: Langmuir atmospheric and astronomical research near South Baldy since the mid-1960s; the research is near the peak, not stated to be on it
evidence.quote: Congress found the mountains uniquely suited for atmospheric and astronomical research which has been conducted at Langmuir Laboratory near South Baldy since the mid-1960s.

evidence.supports: 1980 Langmuir Research Site established by Public Law 96-550
evidence.quote: In 1980, Public Law 96-550 established Langmuir Research Site in the Magdalena Mountains.

evidence.supports: 31,000 acres designated essentially roadless, not wilderness
evidence.quote: The Act designated a 31,000 acre portion of the mountain as essentially roadless, but not wilderness.

evidence.supports: the lookout is filed under the Cibola National Forest

sources.title: Forest Fire Lookouts - New Mexico (by Ron Kemnow)

notes_for_editor: Thin record. Most search results for 'South Baldy lookout' describe a different South Baldy in the Colville National Forest, Washington, with a long lookout history; those are not this site and were not used. A Komoot listing for the Magdalena peak repeats that Washington history, so it was not used. The survey 'Lookouts in the Southwestern Region' has no South Baldy entry. The summit facts come from Wikipedia; the Public Law 96-550 it cites was not opened. The phrase 'near South Baldy' is Wikipedia's wording, not a confirmed summit location. The Magdalena Ranger District (Cibola NF) is the best source for the lookout's history and current status. Two WebSearch calls were used.
